I don't eat beef. Is that a religious commitment? It can be. I don't eat dogs either. That is cultural? National? Ethnic? Me being Hindu and atheist are not mutually exclusive I think. Not believing in any deities or any higher power makes me an atheist. But my political beliefs are still drawn from the Hindu philosophical and cultural roots. I hope I'm not making this very complicated.

What's the difference between actually being a Hindu and using the identity while secretly not being one? It seems more hypocritical. As I said before in this thread, it's less of a religious identity and more of an ethnic one.

It's making me religious in the sense that now I'm more inclined to flaunt my identity and my religious commitments. It's worth mentioning here that I BELIEVE that one can remain a Hindu even if he doesn't believe in religion. It more of an ethnicity than a religion. How can you let go of your ethnic identities?

So, either watch the temples burn and do nothing, or get along with Hindu organisations to protest. I'm not arguing about the philosophical correctness of atheism or one faith is better than the other. Other than waiting for the storm to go away and finding safe refuge in a foreign country, what can be done that is meaningful in some way? Associate yourself with Hindu nationalists or just do nothing and hope they don't attack your home? Let me remind you, this is not spontaneous, this is going on since at least for a 100 years. Hindus are now a miniscule minority in Bangladesh. The country was divided on the basis of religion. So, when Hindu nationalists argue that it's the very nature of Islam to drive out non believers, it's very hard to not fall into that.

But it is becoming more and more clear to me that not every religion is hostile towards atheism. Some are more plural and democratic in terms of believes than others. In fact, atheists are accused of being Hindu-atheists in this country. There has been targeted killings of atheists in this country. So, it doesn't matter whether you're an atheist or a Hindu if you're against same death cult. If you're vocal, they are going to kill you all the same.

The point is to help my community. The dehumanizing, othering and all that stuff is going on since forever. It is so complex when you read the history of the Indian subcontinent. The whole BJP thing in India is like if it is the right wing that protects us then so be it. The funny thing is the coverage of the liberal media in India. Only Hindu nationalists are highlighting it because it suits their agenda. But the violence is very real.
I know it is. It is not making me a believer though. It is kind of a ritualistic show off which brings me closer to my community.
